concept: One magazine feature about one morning: the work you are doing (the plan) sits in a held slot on an editorial page, and a two-column ledger beside it, visible and hidden, accounts for every quick question as units you can count; the page keeps returning, changing state on the spoken word, and typeset pages (headline, term card, table, quiz, habit) print over it or beside it like a magazine's sidebars.

story.metaphor: a ledger: the quick question entered as a cost, one column for what everyone sees and one for what nobody sees
story.setting: two editorial pages on warm paper: the working page (the plan in its slot, the ledger, a time strip running to lunch) and the morning page (the same morning as a grid of time units, with the question slips piling in the margin)
story.arc: hook: the plan unchanged by lunch; setup: the ledger is ruled; turn: one question traced into three hidden parts; reveal: a whole morning, the hidden runs outgrow the visible units, the cost moves to stress and lands on someone else; practice: the viewer predicts which column shrinks; payoff: the same working page returns with the questions batched and the plan further written
story.note: No figure is drawn (decision for the brief's open question): the viewer is 'you', seen only through the work, the slips and the ledger. Editorial pack, D-102: no code-drawn people. The asker in b12 is shown by their page, not their face.

devices.what: the plan held in one slot on the working page (Loom.slot, frame none, rect [200, 150, 760, 780]); it is swapped out for the question and back on the cue words, flickers when you 'answer while writing', and returns as a typeset page (document.page in exactly that rect) for the hunt, the note and the payoff

the two-column ledger, Visible and Hidden, ruled beside the slot; every cost is a unit stamped on its spoken term (Loom.data.stamp cells): ink units for what you see, red runs for what you do not, each run lettered on the thing; it returns set in type (b07) and in the payoff with one short run

the same split applied to a whole morning: a unit grid read like a page (row by row is time), each question stamps one ink unit and a red run, the question slips pile in the margin (Loom.data.pile, counter to five, the spoken hypothetical), runs compress and relabel, then collapse into one
a typeset card (term, quiz, habit) prints over the held page while the page steps back under a paper veil (a template with keep); the page comes forward again untouched in the next beat

a thin time strip across the top of both pages with 'Lunch' at its end; it runs to lunch in the hook, carries the morning in section two, and returns in the payoff with focus time and the agreed time marked on it

join material (fill, every family): a paper object from the frame grows to become the next page; the question slip becomes the headline (b02), the batch tray becomes the closing question (b19). No torn paper or page turns: editorial pack

value_script.why: pale open: warm paper, the plan as the one dark slab, the slip the only accent
the morning page is the densest and richest stretch: the mechanism and the data
the red peaks once: the freed cells fill with red hatch as the cost moves to stress; the most red in the film, kept for that one turn
the check: a pale card over a veiled page, nothing moves through the pause
the answer runs on the morning page: the red runs collapse, so red visibly drains out of the frame
lift for the habits and the close: the opening page returns with almost no red on it

scenes.subject: the plan, held in its slot, as a quick question lands on it
scenes.accent_on: slip: the question mark of 'Quick question?' (the accent marks the question that starts the hidden cost)

design.treatment: An editorial page on warm paper, held still (camera static). Left: the plan in the slot (Loom.slot 'work', frame none, rect [200, 150, 760, 780]) drawn as the plan_page motif: ink page, accent4 header with notebook-pen icon and 'The plan', four lines; line 4 'Next: the budget' is half written, a thin caret at its end. Top: the time strip, a hairline with short ticks from x 200 to 1720, a small ink marker at the left. Right half: bare paper on purpose (the ledger is ruled there in b03); composed negative space, not a drifting block. A slip lands on the plan's top right corner, is answered with a small tick, and the strip's marker runs to 'Lunch' while the plan, and its caret, do not move. The stillness of the plan against the running strip IS the hook.
design.why_motion: two things change and carry the question: time runs along the strip to lunch while the work stays exactly where it was; the contrast between them is the puzzle the lesson answers
elements: strip: the time strip (structure; marker, ticks, 'Lunch' label at the right end)
work: the slot holding the plan page (four lines, caret on line 4)
slip: the question slip, box [760, 190, 420, 150], overlapping the page's top right corner (it is the fill box of b02's join, so it must end the beat exactly there)
answer tick: a small ink tick stamped on the slip
caret: a thin ink caret at the end of line 4

slides in from the right edge and lands on the plan's top right corner, a soft offset shadow under it
'Quick question?' prints on the slip; the question mark is set in the accent

beat_sheet.t_anchor: It takes a minute to answer
beat_sheet.action: the marker steps one tick right (one small step, the minute); a small ink tick stamps on the slip: answered
the marker runs on along the strip to its end (about 2 s, editorial ease); 'Lunch' sets at the right end as it arrives

beat_sheet.t_anchor: is the plan where you left it
beat_sheet.action: nothing in the plan moves: the caret is exactly where it was; a thin ink underline draws under line 4 to point at it, then hold

design.continuity: Geometry is a contract for the whole lesson: slot rect [200, 150, 760, 780] equals document.page (side left) so b04, b17 and b18 land in the same place; the plan_page drawing must match document.page's look (ink page r 18, accent4 header 92 px, icon, title, body lines at y 130 + i x 118 inside the page). The slip ends at [760, 190, 420, 150] with its tick: b02 grows a fill from that box. Name elements exactly: strip, work, slip.

props.title: The visible part, and the hidden one

scenes.rationale: Fill join (the lesson's join material): the question slip from b01 grows to fill the frame in its own paper colour and becomes the headline page; the question literally becomes the subject. A typeset headline, one idea per spread. The kicker echoes the slip's words.

scenes.subject: the slot swapping the plan for the question, and the first hidden cost stamped
scenes.accent_on: hidden run 1: the two red units lettered 'switch cost'

design.treatment: The camera pans down from the headline into the working page, which is re-set exactly as b01 left it (no entrance: the plan in the slot with its caret, the answered slip on its corner, the strip with its marker set back at the first tick, because we now trace that one question). As the pan lands, the ledger is ruled in the bare right half: a header rule and a column rule draw, 'Visible' and 'Hidden' drop in the display serif with the seed's underline label. Then the slot swaps on the spoken words and the first hidden cost is stamped as units. Static camera after the pan.
design.why_motion: the swap is the event being taught (the plan put down for the question), and the cost appears as units at the moment it is named; both are changes over time

work: the slot, swapping the plan out and the question in
hidden_units: three dashed empty run outlines (rows 1 to 3), then row 1 stamped with two red units and lettered 'switch cost'

the caption tag settles beside the dashed rows on a short leader
two red units stamp into row 1 and 'switch cost' letters under them with the accent underline; the footnote fades in at the foot of the ledger

scenes.accent_on: line 4 'Next: the budget' when the highlight finds it
scenes.rationale: Template allocation used as a SHOW, not a card: document.page lands in the slot's exact rect, so the plan slides back into its place, and the highlight moving down its lines on the words IS the hunt for where you were (resumption lag). The ledger stays fully visible beside it (keep, backplate off): visible and hidden side by side. The term is named in the voice and the caption here, and set in type in b07. A gentle push (1.05) toward the page keeps the ledger in frame.

scenes.rationale: Overprint device: the page steps back under the paper veil (keep, default backplate) and the term card prints over it; the page dimming while the term speaks of attention left elsewhere is the picture. Every page element is kept so b06 brings it forward untouched.

scenes.subject: the slot flickering between the plan and the question, each flick a hidden unit
scenes.accent_on: hidden_units row 4: the small red units lettered 'still switching'

design.treatment: The veil recedes and the page comes forward unchanged (hold every kept element). As it clears, before the first word, the ledger catches up with the two terms just defined: rows 2 and 3 of the Hidden column stamp (row 2: four red units, the longest run, lettered 'resumption lag'; row 3: two red units at half opacity, lettered 'attention residue'), and a faint ghost of the slip (opacity 0.15) prints over the plan's top right corner, the residue made visible. Then the slot flickers: the plan page and the question slip alternate in the slot rect by hard swaps, never both at once; each flick stamps one small red unit into row 4.
design.why_motion: the misconception is that answering while writing is doing both; the flicker shows it is switching back and forth, and each switch lands on the ledger as it happens

design.treatment: Hard cut to the morning page: the same strip across the top, and the morning as a unit grid (12 x 6 cells, read row by row like a page: time). Neutral cells are muted outlines. The plan's own work fills cells in accent4 green (the plan's colour, its header band) as the strip's marker advances. Each question stamps one ink unit then a red run of three (the spoken hypothetical 'a few more'), and its slip drops onto a pile in the margin whose counter rides on top (Loom.data.pile, unit box, count 5, from 0 to 5, label 'questions, say'; this beat takes it to 1). A margin note in the caption face states the hypothetical. Static camera.
design.why_motion: the morning is time passing; the grid filling in reading order with the plan's cells, then the first question's ink and red cells, is the accumulation the lesson is about

scenes.subject: the hidden runs compressed by hurrying, the freed space refilled as stress

design.treatment: Hold the grid. Each red run carries a small badge (a Loom.slot, frame badge) reading 'time'. When people speed up, every red run squeezes to about half its width toward its start (the units narrow, one progress drives all five); the freed cells immediately refill with red hatch, so the red total on the page does not shrink. Each badge relabels from 'time' to 'stress'. A caption tag 'One experiment' marks it as a single lab finding.
design.why_motion: the misconception is that hurrying removes the cost; the change shows the cost changing form while its size stays, which only a before and after in place can show

design.treatment: Switch seats without a cut: the held morning (grid, strip, pile) travels right and scales to about 0.55 to become the right-hand page, and a gutter rule draws down the middle: a magazine spread. Then rest on the finished spread.
design.why_motion: the asymmetry is a transaction: one small unit leaves one page and the cost arrives on the other; showing who gives what to whom is the explanation

scenes.subject: the check: which column shrinks if the questions arrive together

props.question: If those questions arrived together, at one agreed time, which column shrinks?

scenes.rationale: Overprint device: the question prints over the veiled morning (keep), so the thing asked about sits behind it; options arrive as peers, the pause ring runs through the 4 s pause, no answer shown. scenes.subject: the morning re-packed: five slips in one batch, one red run, the plan's work joined into one block
scenes.accent_on: the single red run beside the batch

design.treatment: The veil recedes and the held morning travels back to full size (it was the right page). The answer is played on the grid itself: the same five ink units, one red run instead of five, the green work closed up into one long block. A batch slot (Loom.slot, frame card) opens in the margin under the pile, labelled 'agreed time'; the five slips move from the pile into it. The re-pack is a re-flow: cells travel to their new reading-order places (red runs first collapse into one, then the ink units gather at the agreed time, then the green pieces close up), so nothing pops and the counts can be checked by eye. Static camera.
design.why_motion: the answer is a transformation of the picture the viewer predicted on: the same units moved, only the hidden ones removed; seeing them move is the proof that the visible column is unchanged

scenes.subject: the opening page again, with focus time shaded on its time strip and an urgent lane left open
scenes.accent_on: focus_block on the strip (the hatch and its label); red stays only on the one short run

design.treatment: The camera pans back left to the opening page, re-set from the same angle as b01 (callback): the plan in the slot (as in b01, caret on line 4), the strip, the ledger at right now holding the batched morning (Visible: five ink units; Hidden: one short red run of three lettered 'one switch, one return'), and a tray at the foot of the ledger, labelled 'agreed time', with the five ticked slips stacked in it. On that page the habit is drawn on the strip: a block of the morning is shaded in ink hatch and lettered 'focus time', with a narrow open lane at its edge lettered 'urgent route'. The hatch thins when the habit fades and is re-inked on 'Keep it up'.
